text:
For photon–photon pair production, use the invariant energy

\[
s=2E_\gamma \epsilon_{\rm CMB}(1-\cos\theta).
\]

At threshold, the electron and positron are produced with no relative motion in the center-of-momentum frame:

\[
s_{\rm th}=(2m_e c^2)^2=4m_e^2c^4.
\]

The minimum high-energy photon energy occurs for a head-on collision, \(\theta=\pi\), so \(1-\cos\theta=2\). Thus

\[
4E_\gamma\epsilon_{\rm CMB}=4m_e^2c^4
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
E_{\gamma,\min}=\frac{m_e^2c^4}{\epsilon_{\rm CMB}}.
\]

Using \(m_ec^2=5.11\times10^5\ \mathrm{eV}\) and \(\epsilon_{\rm CMB}=10^{-3}\ \mathrm{eV}\),

\[
E_{\gamma,\min}
=\frac{(5.11\times10^5\ \mathrm{eV})^2}{10^{-3}\ \mathrm{eV}}
=2.61\times10^{14}\ \mathrm{eV}
=2.61\times10^5\ \mathrm{GeV}.
\]

No additional factor of two is added for the two final leptons; the factor is already included in the threshold invariant.

Answer: B
